units.title: Human cells: structure and basic properties
units.summary: Typical Human Cell • Cell theory • A cell is the structural and functional unit of life. All living organisms are composed of cells • Human is multicellular organism • Human body is composed of many cells • Over 200 different types of human cells • Types differ in size, shape, and subcellular components; these differences lead to differences in functions Cell Organelles in a Typical Human Cell

Cell Organelles in a Typical Human Cell

units.title: Cell organelles in a typical human cell
units.summary: Cell Organelles in a Typical Human Cell • Plasma membrane (Cell membrane) • Functions: • Separating cytoplasm (intracellular materials) and tissue fluid (extracellular fluid) • Controlling what enters and what leaves cell • Chemicals: • Consists of membrane lipids (Phospholipids and Cholesterols) that form a flexible lipid bilayer • Specialized membrane proteins float through this fluid membrane • Transporter proteins • Channel proteins • Receptor proteins Cell Organelles in a Typical Human Cell • Cytoplasm • All materials inside a cell • Cytosol (Fluid) + Cell organelles (Cellular structures) • Important cell organelles: • Nucleus (Nuclei), • Mitochondrion (Mitochondria), • Endoplasmic reticulum (Smooth / Rough), • Lysosome, • Golgi body Cell Organelles in a Typical Human Cell • Mitochondrion (Mitochondria) • “power plant” of cell • Perform aerobic (oxygen-requiring) cellular respiration to produce most of cell’s energy • Formed by 2 membranes Which type of cell, fat cell or muscle cell, has more mitochondria in cytoplasm? Cell Organelles in a Typical Human Cell • Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) • Membranous organelles extending from the membrane of nucleus • Locate near the nucleus • 2 types:2 • Smooth ER (without ribosome • Rough ER (with ribosome Cell Organelles in a Typical Human Cell • Rough ER • External surface appears rough because of the attached ribosomes • Site of synthesis of proteins and phospholipids • Final protein is enclosed in vesicle and sent to Golgi body for further processing • Smooth ER • Cholesterol and steroid-based hormone synthesis • Converting of glycogen to free glucose • Storage and release of calcium ions

units.title: Primary tissues in the human body
units.summary: Primary Tissues in Human Body • Tissue • Group of cells that are similar in structure and perform common or related function • Four basic tissue types: • Epithelial tissue • Connective tissue • Muscle tissue • Nervous tissue Primary Tissues in Human Body • Epithelial tissue • a sheet of cells that covers body surfaces or cavities • Two main forms: • Covering and lining epithelium: covering external and internal surfaces • example: skin, lining of oral cavity • Glandular epithelium: Secretory tissue in glands • example: salivary glands • Main functions: • Protection of underlying parts • Absorption • Secretion • Sensory reception Primary Tissues in Human Body • Lining epithelium can be divided into 3 types based on their cell shape: • Squamous epithelium • E.g. epidermis of skin • Columnar epithelium • E.g. lining of digestive tract • Cuboidal epithelium • E.g.
